title: Not a canonical EST archive
explain: A .est bundle is a ZIP archive in one exact shape (spec §2): its entries from byte 0, the central directory and its end record straight after, no archive comment, no ZIP64, one disk. Anything else could hide data a reader would skip, so the host refuses it before reading a file.
fix: Pack the bundle with `est pack` (or @cyber-est/tools' `pack`), never with a general ZIP tool, and do not edit the .est afterwards.

title: An entry is not stored plainly
explain: Every entry is stored uncompressed, unencrypted and without a data descriptor, with its sizes in its own header; a directory entry has no data. This keeps one set of files to one archive and lets the plugin origin serve the files as they are.
fix: Pack with `est pack`, which stores every file plainly.

title: Damaged archive records
explain: A local header disagrees with its central directory record, or a record runs past the archive's data: the bundle is damaged or was altered after packing.
fix: Pack the bundle again with `est pack` and copy the new file whole.

title: The bundle is too large
explain: A bundle is at most 64 MiB and 512 entries, and its est.json at most 256 KiB, so an install cannot exhaust the device.
fix: Remove files the plugin does not need (build output, sources, large samples), or shrink them.

title: A path EST does not allow
explain: Paths inside a bundle are relative, `/`-separated segments of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` in UTF-8: no absolute path, no `..` or `.`, no backslash, at most 255 characters. The host serves the files under the bundle's hash, and a path outside these rules could escape it or mean different files on different systems.
fix: Rename the file (letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` only) and pack again.

title: A symbolic link in the bundle
explain: An entry is marked as a symbolic link. A bundle holds files only: a link could point outside the bundle when it is unpacked.
fix: Replace the link with the file itself (copy it) and pack again.

title: A path is in the bundle twice
explain: Two entries have the same path, or paths that differ only in case (which name one file on Windows and macOS).
fix: Rename one of the files so every path is unique ignoring case.

title: est.json is not the first entry
explain: The manifest is the archive's first entry, so a reader finds it without scanning the bundle.
fix: Pack with `est pack`, which writes est.json first.

title: A file does not match its CRC-32
explain: An entry's data does not match the CRC-32 its header records: the bundle was damaged in transfer or altered after packing.
fix: Copy the bundle again, or pack it again with `est pack`.

title: No est.json, or est.json is not JSON
explain: Every bundle has a manifest, est.json, in UTF-8 JSON.
fix: Add est.json at the plugin's root (start from a template's), check it parses, and pack again.

title: A file is in the bundle but not in est.json
explain: Every file in the bundle is listed and hashed in est.json (the module, the UI page or an asset), so nothing unlisted can ride along.
fix: Pack with `est pack`, which lists and hashes every file; or remove the stray file.

title: est.json lists a file the bundle lacks, or lists one twice
explain: est.json names a file (the module, the UI page, an asset or the preset index) that is not in the archive, or names one path twice.
fix: Check the paths in est.json against the plugin folder, then pack again with `est pack`.

title: A file does not match its SHA-256 in est.json
explain: A file's SHA-256 (or the module's size) differs from what est.json records: est.json was written for other files, or a file changed after packing.
fix: Pack again with `est pack`, which fills every hash from the files as they are.

title: The preset index is not valid
explain: The preset index named by est.json's `presets` (spec §6) is a JSON file of at most 64 KiB, `{ "presets": [{ "name", "path", "tags", "stateVersion" }] }`, at most 128 presets, each a state file in the bundle of 1 byte to the inline state limit, with a state version no newer than the manifest's.
fix: Fix the entry the message names in the preset index (write the presets with the template's preset script), and pack again.

title: Not the bundle asked for
explain: The bundle's content hash (the SHA-256 of the archive) differs from the hash the host asked for: a different build, or an altered copy.
fix: Install the bundle by its published hash, or install the file itself in developer mode.

title: A preset's picture or author is not valid
explain: In EST 1.1 a preset in the index may name an `image`, a WebP file in the bundle of at most 64 KiB and 1024 × 1024 pixels (the Presets tab shows it), and an `author` in plain text (60 characters). A 1.0 bundle's presets have neither.
fix: Save the picture as `.webp` (at most 64 KiB, e.g. 256 × 256), put it in `presets/`, and name it by its path; or remove `image`.

title: est.json is not an EST 1 manifest
explain: est.json is a JSON object with `"est": 1`, the manifest schema this host reads (est-manifest-1.schema.json).
fix: Start from a template's est.json, keep `"est": 1`, and point `$schema` at est-manifest-1.schema.json for your editor's completions.

title: The id is not a reverse-DNS id
explain: A plugin's id is a reverse-DNS name of lower-case letters, digits, `.` and `-` (for example `com.example.my-verb`), unique to the plugin and never changed: projects name the plugin by it.
fix: Set `id` to a reverse-DNS name you own, the same in est.json and in the DSP's descriptor.

title: The version is not a semantic version
explain: A plugin's version is a semantic version (`1.0.0`, `1.2.3-beta.1`).
fix: Set `version` to `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`.

title: A text field is missing or not plain text
explain: `name` (60 characters), `vendor` (60), `license` (64) and the optional `description` (400) are plain text without control characters; the optional `url` is an https address.
fix: Fill the field the message names with plain text within its length, or remove the optional one.

title: The kind is neither effect nor instrument
explain: EST 1.0 has two kinds of plugin: `"effect"` (audio in, audio out) and `"instrument"` (notes in, audio out).
fix: Set `kind` to `"effect"` or `"instrument"`.

title: The features list is not valid
explain: `features` is a list of 1 to 32 CLAP feature names whose first is `"audio-effect"` for an effect and `"instrument"` for an instrument.
fix: Start `features` with the kind's feature, then add CLAP's other feature names (`"utility"`, `"stereo"`, `"synthesizer"` …).

title: The ABI editions are not valid
explain: `abi.est` is an EST 1.x edition (`"1.0"`, or since 1.327 `"1.1"`) and `abi.clap` a CLAP 1.x version (`"1.2"`).

title: The module entry is not valid
explain: `module` names the WebAssembly module: a `path` in the bundle, and (filled by the packer) its `sha256` and `bytes`.
fix: Set `"module": { "path": "module.wasm" }` and let `est pack` fill the rest.

title: The UI entry is not valid
explain: An optional `ui` names an `.html` page in the bundle (its `sha256` filled by the packer) and its `size` (`w` 120 to 2000, `h` 80 to 1400), and may say `resizable`.
fix: Set `"ui": { "path": "ui/index.html", "size": { "w": 420, "h": 240 } }`, or remove `ui` for the generated UI.

title: The assets list is not valid
explain: `assets` lists every other file in the bundle with its path and SHA-256 (filled by the packer).
fix: Remove `assets` from your source est.json: `est pack` writes it.

title: The audio ports are not valid
explain: `audio.inputs` and `audio.outputs` each list at most one main port of 1 or 2 channels; an effect needs both. EST 1.1 allows up to 8 channels on a main port and a second input, the sidechain (EST-M021).
fix: Set `"audio": { "inputs": [{ "channels": 2 }], "outputs": [{ "channels": 2 }] }` (an instrument: no inputs).

title: The note ports are not valid
explain: `notes.inputs` and `notes.outputs` are 0 or 1; an instrument needs a note input.
fix: For an instrument set `"notes": { "inputs": 1, "outputs": 0 }`.

title: The limits are not valid
explain: `limits.maxLatencyFrames` (0 to 192000), `limits.memoryPagesMax` (1 to 2048 pages of 64 KiB; default 256) and `limits.tailSeconds` (0 to 60) are whole numbers. They are the most the plugin may use: the host holds it to them.
fix: Set each limit to a whole number in its range, at least what the plugin uses.

title: Permissions asked for
explain: EST 1.0 grants a plugin no permissions (no network, files, devices or clock beyond its own): `permissions` is empty or absent.
fix: Set `"permissions": []` and do the work inside the plugin, or with the host's parameters and state.

title: The parameters list is not valid
explain: `parameters` mirrors the module's parameters, at most 512, each `{ "id", "name", "unit" }` with a whole-number id and a plain-text name (255) and unit (16), and optionally `"scale"`: `"linear"` (the default) or `"log"` (spec §1).
fix: List each parameter the DSP declares, with the same id and name; a `scale` is `"linear"` or `"log"`.

title: The state version is not valid
explain: `stateVersion` is a whole number from 1: the version of the state the plugin saves (a preset names the version it was saved with).
fix: Set `"stateVersion": 1`, and raise it when the saved state's layout changes.

title: The presets entry is not valid
explain: `presets` names the bundle's preset index, a `.json` path in the bundle, listed in est.json like every file.
fix: Set `"presets": "presets/index.json"` and keep the index in the plugin's `presets/` folder, or remove `presets`.

title: A zero-width or direction character in a text field
explain: A text field (the name, vendor, description, a parameter or preset name, a tag) holds a zero-width (U+200B–U+200F) or bidirectional control character (U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069), which can make one name look like another (1.314, EST-14).
fix: Remove the character; write the name as it reads.

title: An EST edition this host does not run
explain: `abi.est` names an EST edition newer than this host runs (Cyber runs EST 1.0 and 1.1). A newer edition can mean things an older host would misread, so the bundle is refused rather than run as if it were 1.0.
fix: Update Cyber, or set `"abi": { "est": "1.1" }` (or `"1.0"`) and keep to that edition's fields.

title: An EST 1.1 field in an EST 1.0 manifest
explain: The manifest uses a field EST 1.1 added (a sidechain input, more than two channels, `modulatable`, `ui.audio`, a preset's `image` or `author`) but says `"abi": { "est": "1.0" }`. A 1.0 bundle keeps 1.0's meaning exactly, so its new fields are refused rather than ignored.
fix: Set `"abi": { "est": "1.1", "clap": "1.2" }`, or remove the field.

title: The sidechain input is not valid
explain: In EST 1.1 an effect may list a second input port after its main one, `{ "role": "sidechain", "channels": 1 }` (or 2): the key Cyber feeds from a track or a return, as it keys its own Compressor. The first port is the main one; only one sidechain, and it follows a main input.
fix: Write `"inputs": [{ "channels": 2 }, { "role": "sidechain", "channels": 2 }]` on an effect.

title: The migrate list is not valid
explain: A version may say what it does with its earlier versions' settings: `migrate` is a list of at most 32 entries `{ from: "<range>", params: { "<old id>": "<new id>" | null }, state: "keep" | "drop" }`. `from` is a version range (comparators separated by spaces, `>=1.0.0 <1.2.0`, a single version, or `*`); every id is a CLAP id as a decimal string and every new id is one the manifest's `parameters` list names (so a manifest with `migrate` lists its parameters); `state` is `keep` (the default) or `drop`. When a project moves a slot to this version, Cyber applies the first entry whose range takes the version moved from: renamed values move, `null` drops, an old id the new version does not know is dropped with a note, and `drop` leaves the saved state behind.
fix: Fix the entry the message names: a range such as `">=1.0.0 <1.2.0"`, ids as strings (`"3": "7"`), a new id that `parameters` lists, and `"state": "keep"` or `"drop"`.

title: Not a WebAssembly 1.0 module
explain: The module is a core WebAssembly binary, version 1 (not a component, not text, not another format).
fix: Build for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` (Rust) or with `asc … --target release` (AssemblyScript), and point est.json's `module.path` at the `.wasm` it writes.

title: A malformed module
explain: The module's sections could not be read (truncated numbers or names, sections out of order, an unknown section or import kind).
fix: Rebuild the module with the template's build; do not post-process it with tools that rewrite sections.

title: A required export is missing
explain: An EST module exports `clap_entry` (a global: the address of its CLAP entry), `malloc` and `free` (functions the host allocates with) and its `memory` (spec §3.1).
fix: Keep the SDK's glue (it exports all four); in AssemblyScript keep `export { clap_entry, free } from "…/est"` and the runtime's `malloc`.

title: The module imports something EST does not allow
explain: A module may import only the WASI functions the host provides (`clock_time_get`, `random_get`, `fd_write`, `proc_exit`, `args_get`, `args_sizes_get`, `environ_get`, `environ_sizes_get` from `wasi_snapshot_preview1`), and nothing else: no `env` functions, no imported memory, table or global.
fix: Remove the code that needs the import (in Rust: `std` I/O, threads, `getrandom`'s JS backend; in AssemblyScript: `Math.random`, which imports `env.seed` (use an xorshift seeded from a constant), `console` and `trace`, `Date`, host bindings, and the runtime's `env.abort` unless it is overridden as the template's asconfig.json does), or build with `#![no_std]` as the template does.

title: Not exactly one table
explain: The module has and exports exactly one function table (growable: the host adds its callbacks to it).
fix: Link with `--export-table --growable-table` (the template's `.cargo/config.toml`; AssemblyScript: `"exportTable": true`).

title: An export uses a name the host reserves
explain: The module exports `refuel` or `fuel_left`, names the host's metering adds.
fix: Rename that export.

title: No memory of its own
explain: The module defines and exports its own linear memory; it may not import one.
fix: Do not link with `--import-memory`; keep the template's link flags.

title: A memory EST 1.0 does not run
explain: EST 1.0 modules have one 32-bit, unshared memory: no memory64, no shared memory (threads), no second memory.
fix: Build for wasm32 without threads or atomics, with one memory.

title: The module's memory is over est.json's limit
explain: The memory's initial size, and its declared maximum, are within est.json's `limits.memoryPagesMax` (and the hard cap of 2048 pages, 128 MiB): the host never lets a module grow past the limit it declared.
fix: Raise `limits.memoryPagesMax` to the module's maximum, or lower the module's (`--max-memory=<bytes>`, AssemblyScript's `maximumMemory`).

title: No memory maximum
explain: The module declares a maximum for its memory, within its limit, so the host can bound it.
fix: Link with `--max-memory=<bytes>` (AssemblyScript: `"maximumMemory": <pages>`), at most `limits.memoryPagesMax` pages.

title: A WebAssembly feature EST does not run
explain: The host meters every module (it counts its work so a runaway loop becomes a trap) and runs only the features the meter knows: the MVP, mutable globals, bulk memory, sign extension, non-trapping conversions, multi-value, reference types and fixed-width SIMD. Relaxed SIMD (its results differ between machines), threads and atomics, exceptions, GC, tail calls, memory64 and multi-memory are refused.
fix: Turn the feature off in the build (Rust: no `+relaxed-simd`, `+atomics`, `+exception-handling` target features; AssemblyScript: the template's `"disable"` list).

title: The module imports env.log_execution
explain: The meter places its counting points through an import of that name; a module that already has it cannot be metered.
fix: Remove the `env.log_execution` import.

title: An instruction the meter does not know
explain: The meter rewrites every function and refuses any expression kind it would otherwise leave unmetered (table and reference instructions among them), rather than run code it cannot bound.
fix: Avoid table and reference instructions (`table.get`, `table.set`, `ref.func` in code …); keep to the SDK's glue for the function table.

title: The module could not be metered or compiled
explain: The meter could not read or rewrite the module, or the metered module did not compile or lost its fuel exports.
fix: Rebuild with the template's settings; if it persists, report the module (with `est inspect`'s output) to the SDK.

title: A start function
explain: The module has a start function. A start function runs when the module is instantiated, before the host can give the metered module any fuel, so it traps. Set-up work belongs in an exported `_initialize()` (the WASI reactor convention, spec §3.1), which the host calls once with fuel before `clap_entry`, or in the plugin's `init` or `activate` (or on the first `malloc`).
fix: Remove the start function and export its work as `_initialize()` instead (Rust: no `#[start]` or constructors; AssemblyScript: no top-level statements with effects, keep `"exportStart"` unset and globals constant, or `"exportStart": "_initialize"`).

title: The module's _initialize trapped or ran out of fuel
explain: A module may export `_initialize()` (the WASI reactor convention, spec §3.1): the host calls it once, right after instantiation and before `clap_entry`, with a block's worth of fuel. It trapped (an `unreachable`, an out-of-bounds access) or did not finish within that fuel, so the plugin cannot start.
fix: Keep `_initialize` to bounded set-up work (tables, constants), move anything long to `activate`, and check it for out-of-bounds writes; run `est test` to see the message.

title: A WASI import with the wrong type
explain: The module imports one of the WASI functions EST allows (`random_get`, `fd_write`, `clock_time_get` …) with a type that is not WASI preview 1's. The host reads an import's arguments by its own types, so a `random_get(f64, f64)` would hand it a length of any size: the import is refused before anything runs (1.314, LR-8b).
fix: Import the function with its preview-1 type (`random_get(i32 buf, i32 len) -> i32`; the SDK's templates and Rust's `wasi` crate do), or do not import it.

title: The plugin does not start
explain: The host could not instantiate the module and create, initialise and activate the plugin through its CLAP entry and factory (the lifecycle order clap-validator checks), or the module trapped while doing so.
fix: Check that est.json's `id` is the descriptor's id, that `init` and `activate` return true, and that nothing traps before the first block (run `est test` and read the phase in the message).

title: The module is not metered
explain: The host runs only metered modules (D-30). The install meters every module itself, so this fails only when a module was run without it.
fix: Install the bundle through the host (or `est validate`), which meters it.

title: The audio ports differ from est.json
explain: The ports the plugin reports (clap.audio-ports) match est.json's `audio`: an effect has a main input and output, an instrument a main output, each with the channel count est.json gives.
fix: Make the DSP's audio ports and est.json's `audio` agree.

title: The note ports differ from est.json
explain: An instrument reports a note input port (clap.note-ports), as many as est.json's `notes.inputs`; any plugin reports as many note outputs as `notes.outputs`, and an effect as many note inputs as `notes.inputs` (a note effect has one of each).
fix: Declare the note ports in the DSP (the SDK's instrument glue declares an input; a note effect's, `export_note_effect!` or `Descriptor.noteEffect()`, one each way) and set `"notes"` to match: `{ "inputs": 1, "outputs": 0 }` for an instrument, `{ "inputs": 1, "outputs": 1 }` for a note effect.

title: A latency over est.json's limit
explain: The latency the plugin reports (clap.latency) is at most `limits.maxLatencyFrames`.
fix: Raise `limits.maxLatencyFrames` to the latency the plugin reports, or report less.

title: A tail over est.json's limit
explain: The tail the plugin reports (clap.tail) is at most `limits.tailSeconds` (one second of grace).
fix: Raise `limits.tailSeconds`, or report the tail the DSP actually has.

title: The parameters are not sane
explain: At most 512 parameters, each id once, each with a finite range (`min` ≤ `default` ≤ `max`).
fix: Fix the parameter the message names in the DSP's parameter declaration.

title: The parameters differ from est.json
explain: The ids the plugin reports (clap.params) are exactly the ids est.json's `parameters` lists.
fix: List every parameter the DSP declares in est.json (same ids), and none it does not.

title: The state is too large
explain: A plugin's saved state is at most 4 MiB (spec §6). The runtime refuses a save past 4 MiB as it is written and answers that the state is too large, which the install names as this rule (and it checks the bytes a save hands back against the same cap).
fix: Save settings, not buffers or caches; rebuild those on load.

title: The state does not round-trip
explain: Saving the state, loading it and saving again gives the same bytes, and the plugin accepts its own state (clap-validator's state round trip). A project reopens the plugin from its state, so anything else changes the sound or loses settings.
fix: Make `saveState` write only what `loadState` reads back (no counters, time or addresses), and `loadState` accept every state `saveState` writes.

title: The plugin stopped while saving its state
explain: The module trapped, or ran out of fuel, inside clap.state's `save` (the install's state check asks once and reads everything the instance posts).
fix: Check the state code for out-of-bounds writes and loops that never end.

title: A bundle preset does not load
explain: Each preset in the bundle is a state the plugin accepts (clap.state `load` returns true).
fix: Write the presets with the plugin's own `saveState` (the template's preset script), at the current state version or one `loadState` migrates.

title: The plugin stopped while processing
explain: The module trapped (an `unreachable`, an out-of-bounds access, a division by zero, a stack overflow) or ran out of fuel (a loop that does not end in time) during the test signal: tones, noise, silence, clicks and every parameter swept by events.
fix: The most common cause in a first plugin is allocating in `render()`: the SDK's heap never gives memory back, so a `new`, an array or a string made each block runs it out. Allocate in the constructor, field initialisers or `activate`, keep every loop bounded by the block, then run `est test` and find the block and the phase in the message.

title: The output is not finite
explain: The plugin wrote NaN or infinity. One NaN in a feedback path silences or destroys a whole mix.
fix: Guard divisions and `log`/`sqrt` against zero and negatives, flush denormals, and clamp feedback below 1.

title: The output is too loud
explain: The output passed +18 dBFS under the test signal (full-scale clicks with every parameter at its extremes). In a project the host clamps every sample it sends to the graph to ±4 (+12 dBFS) and counts what it limited (1.314, "Output limited" on the card), so a loud plugin is bounded; one this loud is refused.
fix: Bound the gain stages (clamp feedback and resonance, limit the output) at every parameter's extremes.

title: An instrument made no sound for a held note
explain: A held note (key 60, velocity 0.8) must reach at least −80 dBFS.
fix: Check note-on handling (the note port, the voice start, the envelope's attack) and that the output is written.

title: An instrument sounds past its reported tail
explain: After a note's release, the output falls below −60 dBFS within the tail the plugin reports (clap.tail): the host stops processing a silent instrument after its tail.
fix: Report a tail at least the longest release, or make the release end within the tail.

title: Two renders differ
explain: Two runs of the same input and events are bit-identical. A project renders the same everywhere (offline export, two peers in a live room) only if the plugin is deterministic; reading `random_get` or the clock in `process` breaks it.
fix: Seed any randomness from a constant (or the state) at `activate`, never from `random_get` or the clock, and keep no state between instances.

title: A preset does not save back its own bytes
explain: A bundle preset, loaded and saved again, gives other bytes. It loads, but a project saved with it differs from the preset.
fix: Write the presets with the plugin's own `saveState` at the current state version.

title: The state could not be saved
explain: Asked for its state, the plugin refused: clap.state's `save` returned false, or the plugin has no clap.state. A project saves every plugin's state; one that cannot be saved loses its settings, so the install refuses it (a trap in the save is EST-C011, a state over 4 MiB EST-C009).
fix: Implement clap.state (the SDK's glue does) and make `saveState` return true.

title: A log parameter's range does not stay above 0
explain: est.json marks the parameter `"scale": "log"`, so knobs, sliders and automation move over its range geometrically (a lane's midpoint is the geometric middle). That needs a continuous range above 0: the range the plugin reports (clap.params) starts at 0 or below, or the parameter is stepped. Only the module knows the range, so the conformance run checks it.
fix: Start the range above 0 (a frequency from 20 Hz, a time from 1 ms), or remove `"scale": "log"` from that parameter in est.json (in the DSP, `.log()` on the builder checks the same).

title: A modulatable parameter is not modulatable in the DSP
explain: est.json marks the parameter `"modulatable": true`, so Cyber's modulators (LFOs, clip envelopes) send it `CLAP_EVENT_PARAM_MOD` events, but the DSP does not flag it `CLAP_PARAM_IS_MODULATABLE` (clap.params): the plugin would ignore them. EST 1.1 (1.327).
fix: Flag the parameter modulatable in the DSP (`.modulatable()` on the builder), or remove `"modulatable": true` from est.json.

title: The note output differs from est.json
explain: est.json says `"notes": { "outputs": 1 }` on an EST 1.1 plugin, so Cyber routes its notes to the next plugin on the track and records them, but the plugin reports no note output port (clap.note-ports), or reports one est.json does not declare.
fix: Declare a note output port in the DSP and set `"notes": { "outputs": 1 }`, or remove both.

title: The UI page is not readable HTML
explain: The page est.json's `ui.path` names is UTF-8 HTML.
fix: Save the page as UTF-8 with an `<html>` element (start from a template's `ui/index.html`).

title: The UI reaches an external host
explain: A plugin UI runs in a sandboxed frame on the plugin origin and may load only files from its own bundle: a URL to another host (`http:`, `https:`, `//host`, `ws:`) in its HTML, scripts or styles would not load, and is refused so a UI cannot phone home.
fix: Copy the file into the bundle (in `ui/`) and refer to it by a relative path; for @cyber-est/ui use the `ui/est-ui.js` that `est pack` copies.

title: A UI URL outside the bundle
explain: Every URL in the UI's HTML, scripts and styles is relative and names a file in the bundle: a root-relative (`/x`) or escaping (`../../x`) URL, or one to a missing file, does not resolve inside the bundle's folder on the plugin origin.
fix: Use a relative path to a file inside the bundle (`ui.js`, `img/knob.png`), and check the file is packed.

title: The UI is large
explain: The UI's files total more than 4 MiB; every install downloads and stores them.
fix: Compress images, drop unused fonts and source maps, and minify scripts.

title: The UI page loads a module script
explain: A UI page with a `<script type="module">`, a `crossorigin` attribute on any element or a `<link rel="modulepreload">` shows a blank frame: the frame's origin is opaque (`sandbox="allow-scripts"`), so a module script, a module preload and a `crossorigin` load are CORS requests, which the plugin origin does not answer. A bundler's default page (Vite's) has all three. (1.335)
fix: Load a classic script: build the app into one `iife` bundle and load it with `<script defer src="assets/app.js">`, with no `type="module"`, no `crossorigin` and no `modulepreload` (see ui.md, "A whole app as the window"; `est new … --app` scaffolds a Vite build that does this).

title: A block costs more than the budget
explain: The mean cost of one 128-frame block in the conformance run, metered, on the validating machine, against a budget of 100 µs (about 4 % of the block's real time at 48 kHz). A warning only in Phase 4: the budget is recorded, not enforced, and the number depends on the machine.
fix: Profile `process`: avoid per-sample divisions, `pow` and `exp` (smooth instead), and recomputing coefficients that have not changed.
